key_insight: FlexAM disentangles appearance and motion by representing video dynamics as a 3D point-cloud control signal, using multi-frequency encoding to capture fine-grained motion while keeping appearance separate for flexible, generalizable video generation control.
problem_solved: Addresses unreliable, task-specific or ambiguous control signals in video generation by providing a clear, modular decomposition of appearance vs. motion that enables interpretable and transferable control across tasks.
method: Represent motion as a 3D point-cloud control signal encoding temporal dynamics across frames.
Apply multi-frequency positional encoding and decomposition to separate fine-grained motion features from appearance information.
Integrate the control signal into a unified FlexAM framework that allows modular conditioning (e.g., swap or mix appearance and motion) for versatile generation and editing.
impact: Offers practitioners a more interpretable, modular way to control video generators—improving transferability, editability, and robustness across tasks such as motion transfer, conditional synthesis, and video editing.
visual_elements: Split diagram showing appearance stream vs. motion (3D point-cloud) stream and their fusion into video output.
Illustration of multi-frequency positional encoding applied to a motion point-cloud (coarse→fine layers).
Before/after examples demonstrating swapping appearance and motion (same appearance + different motion, and vice versa).
Bar or radar chart comparing controllability/generalization of FlexAM vs. baseline methods.
paper_title: FlexAM: Flexible Appearance-Motion Decomposition for Versatile Video Generation Control
paper_authors: Mingzhi Sheng, Zekai Gu, Peng Li, Cheng Lin, Hao-Xiang Guo
